title: Yoga's journey west
hook: a reply built to sting, and the limb that comes before the mat
tomorrow: can you stand up to someone without hating them?

segments.voice: Yesterday, yoga's journey west climbed the Hatha Yoga Pradipika's stairway: the poses as steps to a still mind. Today, what comes before the first step.

A sign-up form at a yoga studio asks about injuries, goals, flexibility. It doesn't ask whether there's a reply sitting in your drafts that's built to sting. The Yoga Sutras would ask that first. Before posture, before breath, Patanjali sets out five restraints for everyday life, and the first one is ahimsa.
screen: `INJURIES, GOALS, FLEXIBILITY.` → `A REPLY BUILT TO STING.` → `FIRST: AHIMSA.`

segments.voice: Sutra 2.30 names the five yamas, the restraints: ahimsa, non-harming; satya, truthfulness; asteya, not stealing; brahmacharya, restraint of desire; and aparigraha, not grasping. In the eight limbs, they come first. Then 2.31 makes them bigger than a class rule: kept everywhere, unbroken by birth, place, time or circumstance, they're called the great vow. Then 2.35, in paraphrase: when someone is firmly established in non-harming, hostility falls away in their presence. Look at what that claims. Not that the non-harming person is safe, or rewarded. That the room changes around them. So ahimsa isn't only not hitting anyone. It reaches into words, and into the reply about to be sent. And it isn't the same as being a doormat. Satya, truth, sits right next to it in the list. A true thing can be said plainly without being made into a weapon. That's the part of yoga that traveled west more quietly. It doesn't photograph well. There's no pose for it. But in the sutras, it's the ground floor, and every other limb stands on it.
screen: `FIVE RESTRAINTS, AHIMSA FIRST.` · `THE GREAT VOW, EVERYWHERE.` · `HOSTILITY FALLS AWAY.` · `TRUE, BUT NOT A WEAPON.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one person you're at odds with right now. Name, silently, what you want from the situation; then the part of you that wants to sting back; then one plain, true sentence you could say that doesn't wound. Give each a few slow breaths.
Yoga's journey west: today, the part that traveled quietly: five restraints, with ahimsa, non-harming, first.
Your line: yoga's journey west. Before the pose, no harm, in deeds and in words. Rest well.
